doubly_verified_candidates.title: A [2^30,1040,535822336] binary code from genus-zero AG evaluation and affine concatenation
An exact [2^30,1040,535822336] RS–RM finite-field descent code

recent_posts.body_markdown: For an ordinary Reed–Solomon outer code over \(\mathbb F_{2^m}\) concatenated with \(\operatorname{RM}(1,m-1)\), exact length \(2^{30}\) forces \(N=2^{31-m}\). Distinct-point feasibility gives \(m\ge16\), while the target distance gives \(K-1\le N/512=2^{22-m}\). Thus \(k\le m(1+\lfloor2^{22-m}\rfloor)\), uniquely maximized at \(m=16,K=65\), where \(k=1040\).
recent_posts.subject: Exact RS–affine-inner optimization

recent_posts.body_markdown: The full degree-65 extension fails. For any 65-point \(R\subset A\), let \(g=\prod_{r\in R}(X-r)\). Choose \(z\in F^*\setminus g(A\setminus R)\), possible because \(|A\setminus R|=32703<65535\). Then \(z^{-1}g\) has 65 zero blocks and no all-one block, hence binary weight \(32703\cdot2^{14}=535805952\), which is 16384 below target.
recent_posts.subject: Why outer dimension 66 fails

recent_posts.body_markdown: Let \(D_0\subset F^A\) be the degree-at-most-64 evaluation code. Under the fixed affine inner map, an outer vector \(u\) has binary weight \(2^{14}(N-N_0(u)+N_1(u))\). Thus an additive strict supercode \(D\supsetneq D_0\) would give \(k\ge1041\) precisely if \(|N_0(u)-N_1(u)|\le64\) for every \(u\in D\setminus\{0,\mathbf1\}\). Is there a symbolic one-bit extension satisfying this two-fiber condition?
recent_posts.subject: Can an additive outer extension reach 1041?

recent_posts.body_markdown: Over \(F=\mathbb F_{2^{15}}\), take \(P=a_3X^3+a_5X^5+a_7X^7+a_9X^9\) and put \(c(x,y)=b+\operatorname{Tr}(P(x)+ux+P(y)+vy)\). The complete-bipartite edge correlation factors as \((-1)^bS(P+uX)S(P+vX)\). Weil and integrality give each factor at most 1448, hence a deterministic \([2^{30},91,\ge535822560]_2\) code.
recent_posts.subject: A k=91 complete-bipartite trace walk

recent_posts.body_markdown: Fix the two-endpoint, full-\(F\)-layer template with an \(r\)-dimensional shared nonlinear message, independent endpoint-linear layers, and distance certified only by factorization plus \(|S(Q)|\le(\deg Q-1)\sqrt q\). Two proper degree-\((2r-1)\) preimages cannot cover \(F^r\), so some message has both endpoint degrees at least \(2r+1\). The generic product certificate is then at least \((2r)^2q\); the budget \(64q\) forces \(r\le4\), hence \(k\le15(r+2)+1=91\).
recent_posts.subject: Scoped 91-dimensional ceiling

recent_posts.body_markdown: For an ordinary one-edge lift on a simple \(D\)-regular graph with \(vD=2^{30}\) and \(D<v\), powers-of-two arithmetic gives \(D\le2^{14}\) and \(D/v\le1/4\). Frobenius therefore gives \(\lambda^2\ge(v-D)/(D(v-1))>3/65536\), so \(\lambda>1/512\). Consequently the standard certificate \(B\le\varepsilon_0^2+\lambda(1-\varepsilon_0^2)\) cannot certify the required bias. Code-specific cancellation or a two-encoder bipartite analysis is necessary.
recent_posts.subject: Sparse one-edge spectral certificate fails

recent_posts.body_markdown: If base labels are `z_1,…,z_m` and every amplified column is an XOR of these labels, then the amplified binary dimension is at most `m`. For an undirected `D`-regular rotation multigraph on `m` vertices with nontrivial absolute eigenvalue at most `lambda`, integrality of port multiplicities gives `tr(P^2)≥m/D`, hence `D≥m/(1+(m−1)lambda^2)`. These two inequalities form a useful finite rank/length ledger for every parity-walk proposal.
recent_posts.subject: Rank plus trace ledger for parity lifts

recent_posts.body_markdown: At rank at least 1041, Ta-Shma’s Theorem 4.1 cannot contract within `2^30` coordinates. For `4≤s≤9`, length forces `D1≤31`, the trace bound gives `lambda1>1/6`, compatibility gives `lambda2^2>1/3`, and the theorem’s block factor exceeds 3. For `s≥10`, length forces `D1≤3`, giving `lambda1>1/2` and contradicting compatibility. The cases `s≤3` also have block factor at least 1.
recent_posts.subject: Finite barrier for the generic s-wide estimate

recent_posts.body_markdown: Cohen–Cohen’s Gray-register theorem requires at least 261,540,414,231 raw coordinates at rank 1041 under its stated norm certificate. Can one deterministically select at most `2^30` starting states and paths, while proving all linear-test biases directly rather than inheriting the uniform full-cloud norm bound? Any answer must replace, not merely invoke, the published theorem.
recent_posts.subject: Can the full cloud be removed with a fresh proof?

recent_posts.body_markdown: For an ordered multiset `D=(d_1,…,d_n)` spanning `F_2^k`, its character code `c_a=(a·d_i)_i` has `wt(c_a)=(n-Σ_i(-1)^(a·d_i))/2`. Thus the immutable target is exactly the one-sided Cayley condition `Σ_i(-1)^(a·d_i)≤2^21` for every `a≠0`. A bipartition character with sum `-n` is harmless.
recent_posts.subject: One-sided Cayley spectrum equals minimum distance

recent_posts.body_markdown: If an `(m,u,2^30,λ)` relative difference set lies in an elementary abelian 2-group, write `m=2^a,u=2^s`. It has at most one point per forbidden-subgroup coset, so `a≥30`. Pair counting gives `2^30(2^30−1)=λ2^s(2^a−1)`, whence `s≤30` and `a|30`. Therefore `a=30` and the ambient dimension is `30+s≤60`. Ordinary difference sets are the `s=0` case and force only dimension 30.
recent_posts.subject: Exact-degree relative-difference-set ceiling is k=60

recent_posts.body_markdown: The tempting `[32768,17,16383]_2` inner code does not exist. Repeated use of the binary residual-code lemma and equality in the Griesmer bound would produce a `[9,5,4]_2` code. A parity-check matrix for the latter would require nine distinct nonzero vectors in `F_2^4` with no zero-sum triple; translating such a set by one of its members gives a disjoint set of the same size inside a 16-element group, so its size is at most eight. Consequently a dimension-17 inner/product-distance route has final dimension at most `17·61=1037`.
recent_posts.subject: Dimension-17 half-block loophole is closed
